correctness.rationale: The t,f values are closed under all five pointwise propositional connectives, including the specified implication (T: T(A) implies T(B), F: T(A) and F(B)) and Boolean negation (the truth table swaps t,f). With a wholly classical operand everywhere, neither b,n nor their conflations occur. The published two-component semantic tests therefore make both b/n essence variants constantly t and both accident variants constantly f for each index. In particular the falsity clause for the complemented accident is true because every world avoids the conflated index; this is needed for the induction on arbitrary nesting. At a fixed root the entire restricted language depends only on the atomic values at that root. For a t/f/T/F target its exact-value or component test agrees with the corresponding classical test. Make that test true at the root for the plain variants and false for the complemented-test variants. The target essence is true in the constant model and false when the other world is flipped, and its accident counterpart reverses that truth bit. The falsity clauses also give the complementary classical bits in these cases. The models agree on every root atom, including extra variables, so the obstruction rules out even designated-truth-only definitions. A counterexample among universal two-world models suffices against a definition required on the entire S5 class.
residual_risks: The induction uses wholly classical atomic assignments only as witnesses, not as a characterization of arbitrary four-valued models. It does not address extra primitives or signatures outside the statement.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Classical output is weaker than independence from other worlds. Normal forms allowing ordinary-status operators do not prove what can be expressed without them. Broader embeddings or results about different primitives therefore do not settle the restricted separation as inspected.
